answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by binding each identity to a sequential cipher river: a memory-hard chain where every step hashes the prior private state with a unique basalt-derived salt that cannot be precomputed or shared. Spawning N fakes requires N independent sequential rivers; because each hash depends on the previous, attackers cannot parallelize or pool the work across clones, forcing wall-clock time and dedicated memory to scale at least linearly with identity count. Honest agents incur the cost once; farms pay per head.
